drivingQuestion: From where is it derived that only known impurity negates a nazirite's term?
outcomeNote: both verse derivations set aside for an oral tradition

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי? אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״וְכִי יָמוּת מֵת עָלָיו בְּפֶתַע פִּתְאֹם״, ״עָלָיו״ — בִּמְחֻוֶּורֶת לוֹ.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» The Gemara asks: «From where are these matters» derived, that there is a difference between known and unknown impurity? «Rabbi Eliezer said that the verse states» with regard to a nazirite: «“And if any man shall die very suddenly beside him”» (Numbers 6:9). The emphasis provided by the term «“beside him”» indicates «that» it is «clear to him» that he has become impure. However, one is not impure if the presence of the corpse is unknown.

segments.he: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: אָמַר קְרָא ״כִּי יִהְיֶה טָמֵא לָנֶפֶשׁ אוֹ בְדֶרֶךְ רְחֹקָה״. כִּי דֶרֶךְ: מָה דֶּרֶךְ בְּגִלּוּי, אַף כֹּל בְּגִלּוּי.
segments.en: «Reish Lakish said» a different source: «The verse states» with regard to the Paschal offering: “Any man of you «who shall be ritually impure due to a corpse or on a road far away”» (Numbers 9:10). The word “road” is juxtaposed in the verse to the term “ritually impure,” indicating that the impurity is «like a road. Just as a road is in the open, so too, every» impurity is «in the open.» It must be a known impurity.

segments.he: וְאֶלָּא הָדִתְנַן: אֵיזוֹהִי טוּמְאַת הַתְּהוֹם — כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַכִּירָהּ אֶחָד בְּסוֹף הָעוֹלָם. אֲבָל מַכִּירָהּ אֶחָד בְּסוֹף הָעוֹלָם — אֵין זוֹ טוּמְאַת הַתְּהוֹם.
segments.en: The Gemara objects: «But» consider «that which we learned» in the Tosefta (Zavim 2:9): «Which is the ritual impurity» imparted by a grave «in the depths?» It is impurity imparted by «any» corpse «of which no one is aware,» even «at the end of the earth.» This type of impurity is permitted for both a nazirite and one who sacrifices the Paschal offering. «However,» if even «one» person «is aware of it,» even «at the end of the earth, this is not impurity» imparted by a grave «in the depths.»

segments.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר כִּי דֶרֶךְ — שַׁפִּיר. אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר — בִּמְחֻוֶּורֶת לוֹ, כִּי מַכִּירָהּ אֶחָד בְּסוֹף הָעוֹלָם מַאי הָוֵי?
segments.en: The Gemara states its question: «Granted, according to the one who says» that this halakha is derived from the verse that states that ritual impurity is «like a road,» it is «fine,» as an item known to someone in the world can be compared to a road. «However, according to the one who says» that this halakha is derived from the term “beside him,” i.e., it is referring «to» an impurity that is «clear to him, if one» person «at the» other «end of the earth is aware of» this impurity, «what of it?» It was unknown to the nazirite himself.

segments.he: וְתוּ, הָא דְּתַנְיָא: הַמּוֹצֵא מֵת מוּשְׁכָּב לְרׇחְבָּהּ שֶׁל דֶּרֶךְ, בִּתְרוּמָה — טָמֵא, בְּנָזִיר וּבַעֲשִׂיַּית פֶּסַח — טָהוֹר. מַאי שְׁנָא? אֶלָּא טוּמְאַת הַתְּהוֹם גְּמָרָא גְּמִירִי לַהּ.
segments.en: «And furthermore,» consider «that which is taught» in another baraita (Tosefta, Zavim 2:8): In the case of «one who finds a corpse lying» across «the width of a road,» i.e., it had been buried there in such a way that it was impossible for the passerby to avoid becoming impure by passing over the corpse, then «with regard to teruma,» the passerby is «impure.» Therefore, if he is a priest, he may not eat teruma. However, «with regard to» both being «a nazirite and» being «one performing» the ritual of «the Paschal offering,» the passerby is «pure. What is different» about these situations? «Rather,» it must be that the halakha of «impurity» imparted by a grave «in the depths is learned as a tradition» and not from the verses, which are cited merely in support.
